elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall ...", so all three limbs (a)-(c) are triggered by either expiry or termination, however arising.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — obligation sits on TrueLink (Vendor) and matches the six-month ceiling.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) ends "at TrueLink's then-current rates", which is the playbook pricing basis and avoids an open-ended free-services commitment dispute.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days, return all Client Content and other Client data"; the 30-day clock is anchored to the opening "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return "in a commonly used, machine-readable format", tracking the model language.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "thereafter delete such Client Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing" — deletion is sequenced after return ("thereafter") and certification is written.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) makes assistance available "for up to six (6) months", an availability window that exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Client Content and other Client data within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination, in machine-readable form.

reasons: Finding kind "missing" is corroborated: Sections 13 and 14 as originally drafted contain no vendor-side exit obligation — Section 14 only extends service through the month following notice, and Section 13 places the migration burden entirely on Client (new name server in 30 days, new hosting environment in 60 days) with no return, export, deletion or assistance mechanic.

The single inserted paragraph in Section 14 renders all six preferred elements in operative language (trigger, six-month assistance, then-current rates, 30-day return, commonly used machine-readable format, post-return deletion plus written certification); the preferred checklist is therefore complete and the fallback checklist is subsumed.

Terminology is correctly localised to this Agreement: "Client Content and other Client data" is used instead of the undefined "Customer Data", and the obligor is TrueLink, so no undefined trigger or dangling defined term is introduced.

Minimal: one concise insertion, no deletion or rewording of existing text, no duplication of an existing operative term (none exists), and no added requirements outside the TRANSITION checklist (e.g. no free-of-charge assistance, no escrow, no audit right).

Preserves intent: Section 13's Client-side 30/60-day arrangements for a new name server and hosting environment and Client's retained domain/Client Content ownership survive unchanged and do not contradict a TrueLink assistance-and-return duty; Section 14's month-end wind-down of Hosting and Support Services is untouched; Section 24's survival of Sections 5–30 carries the new Section 14 obligation past termination as the rationale states.

No repair required. Optional (rationale-level only, not a deviation): the clause is silent on whether assistance must be requested before termination and on any cap on the then-current rate uplift — acceptable under the playbook's minor sub-element treatment.
